THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING  IN B GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  WP No. 13417 of 2022  ORDER
The short grievance of the Petitioner-land loser is as to non-extension of the benefit of enhancement of compensation in terms of Section 28A of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

2. Learned counsel for the Petitioner argues that by the very scheme of the said section, wherever there is enhancement of compensation u/s 18 of the 1894 Act on reference, the benefit of enhancement has to be extended to all those lands comprised in the very same notification and this having not been done, despite representation, he says, his client is more than justified in complaining to the Writ Court.

3. After service of notice, the Respondent having entered appearance through his Advocate, oppose the Petition contending that the enhancement of compensation has been made u/s 18 reference is true, however, those awards have been put in challenge before this Court in Miscellaneous First Appeals and interim stay has also been obtained subject to payment of 50% of the enhanced amount.
That being the position, it is difficult to grant relief to the Petitioner in terms of the prayer made herein.

4. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition Papers, this Court is of a considered opinion that the representation made by the Petitioner merits consideration at the hands of Respondent-Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO) in terms of compensation granted by the Reference Court by virtue of award made u/s 18(1).
However, actual disbursal of the compensation would depend upon the outcome of the MFAs and this view is shared by learned counsel for the Petitioner, as well.

In the above circumstances, the Respondent-Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO) is directed to consider the representation of the Petitioner within a period of three months, keeping in view the observations hereinabove made and subject to outcome of the appeals in M.F.A.No.6323/2021 &
connected matters
, all contentions in this regard are kept open.
It is open to the answering Respondent to solicit any information/documents from the side of the Petitioner for due consideration of his Representation.
However, in the guise of such solicitation, no delay shall be brooked.
No costs.
